Results.ReviewText:
After 5+ years, the ignition system stopped working. The website was very clear on how to analyze the problem. The customer service attendant was polite and efficient. [She had my records dating back to the previous Weber grill I bought around 2004, and the one I inherited before that!] Weber sent a replacement kit—new switch, new wires, new clips, even a new AA battery—and very clear instructions on how to replace the old one. Replacement took a careful 30 minutes, and now the unit works like new!

Years ago, I found an old Weber left behind when I bought an apartment. It wasn’t working. I called Weber and even though I was not the original purchaser, they sent replacement parts, again without any hesitation. 

The cost for these repair kits? Zero. And Weber paid the shipping, too.

I will be a proud Weber customer for life.
Results.Title: Amazing warranty—and they MEAN it!

Thank you for your feedback. Your satisfaction is very important to us. So sorry to hear about your side tables getting hot.  We always recommend wearing a BBQ mitt when using the grill for safety reasons. All parts of the grill can get hot when in use. 

Regarding the knobs, the 12 o'clock position is off. Same as a stove in the house the knobs always start at 12, when moving to 9 that is the start/high position. Hope this helps. If you need any further assistance please reach out direct. We are always happy to help. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText:
i used the Grill twice. The first time I noticed that the side shelves were very hot. The prior Weber grill I had for more than 10 years came with wooden slats. They did not conduct 'heat' ...not only did they look beautiful, but they were always cool to the touch.... not like the one I have now. My suggestion is to provide a 'Covering 'Mat' for each side... which would be fireproof & and would dissapait the heat. 

The 2nd time i used the grill, it barely provided sufficient heat. I immediately realized I must have initiated Weber's "safety protocol" which prevents the grill from heating up. I realized I had positioned the burner knobs  incorrectly. Since i had not used the grill for a few weeks, i forgot 'your' "Code" for positioning the knobs. SINCE THEY ARE NOT LABLED e.g,, LOW  - MEDIUM -HIGH, but 
only include cryptic diagrams of the heat volume, I mispositioned them. I had to review the instructions to figure out where exactly to position the knobs, and I was therefore able to start the grill properly.

. I would hope in the future that you would help out those who ' don't remember'to include LOW -MEDIUM & HIGH on your machine.
AND TO CLARIFY WHERE EXACTLY TO POSITION THE KNOBS WHEN STARTING THE GRILL.
Results.Title: Mike

ClientResponses.Response:
Your feedback means a lot to us. We are so sorry to hear your about your hose and regulator leaking. We are here to help. 

In almost every case of reported leaks, the rubber gasket on the inside of the propane tank nozzle is oval in shape, as opposed to round, is cracked or is otherwise compromised, and therefore results in a leak. The gasket should be perfectly round, with no nicks or cracks.

Be sure to visually inspect that all the burners are extinguished (No Flame Present).

Our Care team will reach out to follow up. Please look for an outreach email from us soon. Thank you!
